historicalOrigins.previousUse: The analysis selected exact completion-referenced records by phase and kept missing pointers, unresolved pointers and ambiguous candidates distinct. The _md type did not change the content wire type.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Those selection and availability rules feed INVESTIGATION_RESULT Projection, while JournalRecord stays the native envelope.

invariants: Scope is AgentSpace plus Execution plus native record ID.
Do not assume content.markdown, content.text or a fixed root-cause schema.
Investigation and mitigation summaries are separate phases.
No native single-record GetJournalRecord operation is inferred from the application getter.

entities.purpose: A retained application record of an observed DevOps approval request context, including its native approval identity, execution, exact request evidence and action digest. It is a control/audit entity, not evidence that a tool ran successfully.
entities.ownership: The collector owns request content and observed rawState. DecideApproval and ResumeExecution admit separate Commands under current authorization and exact request context; local clients cannot set provider approval state directly.
entities.lifecycle: Observed request/state changes publish ApprovalRequest versions. Decision and resume Command identities are retained independently, allowing partial success or an ambiguous response to remain visible. Neither decision acceptance nor resumption proves the intended operational result.

useCases.title: Approve a precisely observed action
useCases.scenario: An execution pauses with a validated approval request.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Review its exact actionDigest and request Source, then submit DecideApproval against that context.
useCases.outcome: The accepted decision is auditable without broadening its scope or assuming action execution.

useCases.title: Recover decision success with failed resume
useCases.scenario: The approval call succeeds but the resume response is lost or fails.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Keep decisionCommandIds and resumeCommandIds distinct and inspect their reconciled outcomes before any new action.
useCases.outcome: The UI preserves partial success and uncertainty rather than showing a false completed action.

historicalOrigins.heading: 5. Actions, approvals and operator decisions
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The earlier UI contract modeled an observed request context around native approval values, then separate UpdateApprovalAction decision and SendMessage resumption stages. Space-scoped approvalId was separate from interrupt/tool/execution context.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: ApprovalRequest remains the observed request entity. DecisionAttempt and ResumeAttempt consolidate into Command, with ordinary entity versions and no implied single-execution limit on reusable native approval identity.

invariants: Preserve actual native approval, interrupt and tool-use context; a button label is not identity.
A successful rejection is different from a failed API request.
Approval redemption or decision acceptance does not prove successful tool execution.
Lost approval/resume responses require a verified recovery path, not blind mutating replay.

entities.purpose: A native DevOps asset root with ordinary entity versions. Each retained Asset representation selects an exact nativeVersion, Source and owned file descriptors, allowing historical content to be addressed without a separate AssetVersion entity.
entities.ownership: The collector owns the observed metadata, native version and file evidence. assetType is open provider content; documented metadata profiles remain qualified source interpretation rather than arbitrary writable fields on the canonical entity.
entities.lifecycle: Observed native metadata/content versions publish Asset versions under the same assetId. The application version and nativeVersion are separate. A historical read uses exact file/artifact references and reports unavailable content rather than substituting the provider’s latest alias.

useCases.title: Reopen an attached checklist
useCases.scenario: An investigation references a skill or attachment that has since changed.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Use the captured Asset version and exact nativeVersion/file evidence retained for that historical context.
useCases.outcome: The original reviewed content is reproducible if retained and authorized, instead of being replaced by current files.

useCases.title: Separate available context from consumed inputs
useCases.scenario: The AgentSpace contains skills and memories while an execution runs.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Retain asset availability/configuration with provenance and record actual consumption only when source evidence supports it.
useCases.outcome: The UI does not claim that every available current asset was used by the historical execution.

historicalOrigins.heading: 8. Artifacts, assets and reproducibility
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The earlier model kept native assets/files distinct from journal content and A2A artifacts and required a specific assetVersion for reproducible historical reads.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: AssetVersion is no longer an independent entity or nested independent history array. Asset uses the same identity/version contract as all entities, with nativeVersion and files as fields of the selected representation.

historicalOrigins.heading: Documented Asset profiles
historicalOrigins.previousUse: Documented metadata could link custom agents to skills/memory stores, memories to stores and feedback to executions, without proving historical consumption.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: The consolidation retains these as source-backed native profiles and preserves availability, attachment and consumption as different claims.

invariants: Native version is not the application entity version.
Files are owned values under the selected Asset version.
A journal URI or A2A artifact ID is not automatically a native assetId.
Current asset availability does not prove historical consumption.

entities.purpose: One application-authored workflow definition with a stable identity and DRAFT, PUBLISHED or ARCHIVED representations. A Scenario owns step definitions, operation locks, checks and publication metadata; versions express publication history without a separate ScenarioRevision entity.
entities.ownership: Application authoring commands own the definition. PublishScenario validates and freezes the complete executable contract, schemas, expression/reducer rules and immutable operation locks under the Scenario version. Owned step definitions have no independent CRUD lifecycle.
entities.lifecycle: CreateScenario begins a draft; UpdateScenario appends a draft representation; PublishScenario appends a PUBLISHED representation with its digest. Editing a published or archived definition creates a later DRAFT without changing old publications. ArchiveScenario appends an ARCHIVED head that blocks new admissions, while exact replay of an already admitted Run preserves its receipt.

useCases.title: Publish a repeatable fault exercise
useCases.scenario: An author defines a fault action, workload checks and finalizers.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Publish the Scenario so every operation alias resolves to an exact retained implementation/schema lock and the check definitions are frozen.
useCases.outcome: A Run can select a reproducible program rather than whichever implementation an alias points to later.

useCases.title: Revise without changing earlier runs
useCases.scenario: The author adjusts the error-budget check after one run has finished.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Create a later DRAFT and then publish another Scenario version; earlier Runs keep their exact PUBLISHED reference.
useCases.outcome: Definition evolution does not rewrite the criteria or behavior of an admitted run.

historicalOrigins.heading: 1. Entities, ownership and identity
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The earlier workflow split mutable Scenario catalog metadata from immutable ScenarioRevision configuration, with definitions and complete dependency locks owned by each revision.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: ScenarioRevision is folded into Scenario. Draft editing, publication and archival now append ordinary Scenario versions under one identity; owned values inherit that version.

historicalOrigins.heading: 2. Publication and admission
historicalOrigins.previousUse: Publication resolved aliases and retained implementation/schema contracts; admission rejected missing or revoked pinned artifacts rather than silently substituting current aliases.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Those invariants remain, with Run selecting EntityRef(Scenario,id,version) instead of a separate revision ID.

invariants: A published Scenario version is immutable.
New drafts do not invalidate explicit selection of an older PUBLISHED version; a current ARCHIVED head blocks new admission.
A FIS ExperimentTemplate is provider configuration, not automatically a Scenario.
A digest establishes declared content integrity, not external cloud immutability or permission.

entities.purpose: An admitted execution of one exact published Scenario version, with a frozen input Snapshot and an explicitly selected history of StepRuns. Run keeps orchestration, acceptance, finalization and external-effect state separate.
entities.ownership: The workflow runtime owns Run lifecycle publications. StartRun performs trusted admission; RequestRunCancellation records monotonic control intent. Clients cannot set executionOutcome, assessmentVerdict or runtime status through a generic update.
entities.lifecycle: Admission pins the PUBLISHED Scenario, resolved bindings, enabled steps and required criterion denominator before dispatch. State transitions append Run versions. Cancellation fences new main dispatch while existing effects are reconciled. Terminal Run facts are sealed; later observations or new evaluation Projections do not rewrite the admitted execution.

useCases.title: Execute a published checkout exercise
useCases.scenario: An operator starts a known Scenario version against captured workload bindings.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Read the Run’s exact scenario, inputSnapshot and pinned StepRun references as its runtime progresses.
useCases.outcome: The console can explain what was admitted and which exact child representations produced a displayed result.

useCases.title: Cancel while the remote effect is uncertain
useCases.scenario: A fault-start request may have reached AWS but its response was lost.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Record cancellation intent, reconcile the originating dispatch and use finalization/effect dimensions to retain unresolved remote work.
useCases.outcome: The Run can terminate with an indeterminate effect state rather than falsely reporting that cancellation restored the workload.

historicalOrigins.heading: 1. Entities, ownership and identity
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The earlier Run owned admission context, cancellation, steps and attempts and pinned one ScenarioRevision. Its final result was sealed.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Run now has an ordinary entity version, pins a Scenario version and a shared Snapshot, and records exact child versions rather than latest-only child IDs.

historicalOrigins.heading: 4. Execution and assessment are separate facts
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The workflow model separated technical outcome, required-check verdict, finalization and unknown remote effects. An empty required set was not automatically passed.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: The same dimensions remain explicit on Run; independent projectionVersion counters are removed in favor of Run.version.

historicalOrigins.heading: 5. Retries, cancellation and finalization
historicalOrigins.previousUse: Cancellation fenced further main dispatch, cleanup had a separate finite budget and unresolved effects remained indeterminate rather than hidden as normal cancellation.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: These remain Run-owned control and state semantics with versioned command receipts and retained effect evidence.

invariants: Run pins an exact PUBLISHED Scenario and RUN_INPUT Snapshot.
Runtime skipping or cancellation cannot shrink the admitted required-criterion denominator.
No required criteria means NOT_EVALUATED, not automatic success.
A finished Run or passed verdict does not establish remote cleanup.
Run.steps references exact StepRun versions; historical reads cannot join current child heads.

entities.purpose: The Run-owned lifecycle of one named Scenario step, including a step that never executes. It provides the scheduling outcome, explicit attempt selection and exact retry history without becoming an independently editable workflow definition.
entities.ownership: The workflow runtime owns StepRun. Its uniqueness includes runId and stepKey; Scenario owns the corresponding StepDefinition value. There is no independent retry, status-edit or step-authoring command for StepRun.
entities.lifecycle: Runtime transitions publish StepRun versions. attempts retains exact StepAttempt references and selectedAttempt states which result drives the step’s interpretation. A skipped step can validly have zero attempts, with a reason retained. The parent Run selects the exact StepRun versions used by that representation.

useCases.title: Explain a zero-attempt skipped check
useCases.scenario: A required check cannot run because an upstream action failed.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Retain its StepRun with skipReason and zero attempts rather than deleting it.
useCases.outcome: The required criterion remains visible and cannot disappear from the Run denominator.

useCases.title: Inspect a permitted retry
useCases.scenario: A read-only query is retried under the published bounded retry policy.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Keep both attempt references and explicitly select the attempt used by the step result.
useCases.outcome: The UI can explain retry history without confusing transport polling with a new workflow step.

historicalOrigins.heading: 1. Entities, ownership and identity
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The prior workflow had exactly one StepRun for every compiled main/finalizer step, even if never attempted, with no independent retry/status mutation API.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: The entity is retained and uniformly versioned. attempts and selectedAttempt pin exact child representations rather than implicit current records.

historicalOrigins.heading: 4. Execution and assessment are separate facts
historicalOrigins.previousUse: Earlier step summaries selected actual attempts under the retry policy while technical and assessment outcomes stayed separate.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: StepRun now uses its common entity version instead of a special projection history mechanism.

invariants: StepRun is runtime state, not the authored StepDefinition.
One Run/stepKey identifies the step; retries are StepAttempts.
Zero attempts is valid for a skipped step.
Selecting an attempt does not discard earlier attempts or unresolved effects.

entities.purpose: One durable execution attempt of a StepRun, with a stable dispatch identity, observed external effects, exact evidence and optional check result. It is the record that makes retry and uncertain-effect handling concrete.
entities.ownership: The workflow runtime owns attempt facts. attemptNo counts deliberate retries and is distinct from StepAttempt.version. ExternalOperationRef and CheckResult are owned values; their provenance and remote disposition remain explicit.
entities.lifecycle: The dispatch key is persisted before any provider call. Polling, transport recovery and checkpoint resume stay within the same attempt; a permitted deliberate retry creates another attempt only after the previous effect is reconciled. Lifecycle versions accumulate until settlement, after which attempt facts are sealed. Late reconciliation adds new evidence rather than rewriting the settled attempt.

useCases.title: Reconcile a lost FIS start response
useCases.scenario: A worker loses contact after dispatching the FIS start request.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Use the retained dispatchKey and external-operation intent to investigate the existing effect through a supported non-creating recovery path.
useCases.outcome: The engine avoids launching a second fault merely to discover whether the first exists.

useCases.title: Retain a conclusive check result
useCases.scenario: A workload query supplies sufficient evidence for a required assertion.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Store the result with evaluator/predicate identity, cutoff and exact evidence references on the settled attempt.
useCases.outcome: The result can be audited without treating later samples or a new evaluator as part of the original check.

historicalOrigins.heading: 1. Entities, ownership and identity
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The earlier attempt was scoped by Run, step and attempt number, appended dispatch/checkpoint/effect facts during execution and sealed terminal facts.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: StepAttempt retains its own identity and common version metadata; attemptNo remains an execution-order fact.

historicalOrigins.heading: 5. Retries, cancellation and finalization
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The workflow required persisted dispatch intent before calls, reconciliation before mutating retry and explicit indeterminate outcomes for unresolved effects.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Those safeguards remain with exact entity/evidence references and no exception to universal versioning.

historicalOrigins.heading: 6. Evidence and assertions
historicalOrigins.previousUse: Assertions froze evidence IDs, evaluator contracts and cutoff; unavailable or insufficient evidence could not establish conclusive absence, and later data could not silently rewrite a sealed result.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Shared Source/Observation/Projection evidence replaces a separate generic Evidence entity while settled attempt facts stay sealed.

invariants: Persist dispatch intent before the external call.
A timeout or lost handle does not establish that the remote effect did not happen.
A new mutating attempt is forbidden while the earlier effect is unresolved.
A false assertion is not a retryable technical error.
Sealed facts remain unchanged; later reconciliation is separately retained evidence.

entities.purpose: One native AWS FIS experiment, independently observable whether or not the console launched it. It retains runtime configuration/evidence, named action values, selected target memberships, resolution coverage and report state.
entities.ownership: The FIS collector owns observed experiment representations. Native actions, dependencies, selector bindings, target accounts and reports remain provider-owned values under Experiment rather than independent console StepRuns or controllable action entities.
entities.lifecycle: Accepted provider observations publish Experiment versions under the scoped native identity. The historical run is interpreted from its retained runtime configuration and template provenance, never from current mutable template contents. StopExperiment records asynchronous intent; subsequent observed status and independent workload/effect evidence establish what followed.

useCases.title: Inspect a workflow-launched fault
useCases.scenario: A StepAttempt starts FIS and retains its external experiment identity.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Follow that evidence to Experiment while keeping the console Run/StepRun graph separate from native named actions.
useCases.outcome: The operator sees both orchestration and provider execution without fabricating independent action controls.

useCases.title: Compare selected scope with observed recovery
useCases.scenario: An experiment completes and its report later becomes available.
useCases.howEntityIsUsed: Inspect targetMemberships, resolutionCoverage, actions and report independently, then evaluate workload telemetry through Projection.
useCases.outcome: Selected targets, action completion, report readiness and workload recovery remain separate evidence-backed claims.

historicalOrigins.heading: 2. Core execution model
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The FIS analysis centered on the native experiment and named action map keys, preserving same-experiment dependency/binding scope and the runtime configuration snapshot.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Experiment remains the native entity. Named action/runtime members are owned values, and universal Experiment versions replace any special state-history classes.

historicalOrigins.heading: 5. Target selectors, resolved memberships, and accounts
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The prior model retained every selector membership, complete targetInformation and separate resolution-ended versus page-traversal evidence; configured target accounts were not child experiments or per-account results.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: Experiment retains memberships and qualified coverage; optional canonical Resource resolution is evidence-based, and shared Collection/Source/Observation retain the collection mechanics.

historicalOrigins.heading: 7. FIS and operator UI mapping
historicalOrigins.previousUse: The generalized workflow treated an experiment as an external execution of a StepAttempt and native action detail as provider-owned, while reports and checks had independent lifecycles.
historicalOrigins.consolidation: That boundary is preserved: Run can refer to zero, one or several Experiment identities, and workload acceptance remains a Projection rather than a native experiment field.

invariants: No individual native action stop, retry or pause operation is invented.
Named action identity is experiment plus action name, not catalog actionId.
Selected membership does not prove a per-resource fault occurred.
A stopped experiment does not prove workload recovery.
Report availability is independent of experiment outcome and acceptance verdict.
